title: Soya Group launches FLOW Maritime
summary: Soya Group's FLOW Maritime launches, aiming to help shipowners "unlock value" from alternative fuels by integrating compliance and environmental attributes. This service appears designed to optimize FuelEU Maritime pooling and regulatory costs, rather than driving immediate, substantial reductions in carbon intensity from high-emitting vessels. While managing compliance is crucial, the focus remains on financial "value" and "attributes," raising skepticism about the actual, quantifiable impact on global HFO consumption and CO2 output.
content:
Soya Group is now launching FLOW Maritime, a new marine energy transition company established to help shipowners realise the commercial, regulatory and environmental value of moving to alternative fuels. FLOW Maritime supports the wider maritime sector in accelerating its decarbonization journey, serving as a catalyst for faster decarbonization across the global maritime industry.

The transition to lower-carbon shipping is creating a rapidly evolving commercial landscape. Fuel supply, certification, regulatory compliance and environmental markets are increasingly interconnected, yet often managed separately.

FLOW Maritime was established to bridge that gap.

By combining alternative fuel portfolio management, certified chain of custody, FuelEU pooling and environmental attributes in an integrated commercial model, the company helps customers unlock more of the value created through lower-carbon operations.

“Shipping companies are under growing pressure to reduce emissions, but the business case for doing so is often assessed too narrowly,” says Daniel Gent, Managing Director of FLOW Maritime. “The price of the fuel is only one part of the equation. When compliance value, emissions reductions and environmental attributes are considered together, the economics can look very different.”

Although FLOW Maritime is a new company, it is built on an established foundation. As part of Soya Group, the company benefits from an owner with deep roots in shipping, a long-term perspective and extensive experience of developing businesses and innovations within the maritime sector.

“The energy transition will require long-term relationships built on trust,” says Daniel Gent. “Shipowners need partners that combine expertise with transparency, reliability and a genuine commitment to the future of the industry. Being part of Soya Group gives us that foundation from day one.”

Transparency and traceability will be central to FLOW Maritime’s approach. Through robust certification processes, documented chain-of-custody management and clear governance, the company aims to provide customers with confidence that the environmental and commercial value they depend on is credible, verifiable and responsible.
